subject: biology

moments.title: Priestley restores air
moments.body: Priestley puts a mouse in a sealed jar — it dies. He adds a sprig of mint — and the mouse can live. Plants 'restore' air. He doesn't know that what plants produce is oxygen.
moments.takeaway: Plants change the air. We now know they produce oxygen.

moments.title: Ingenhousz adds sunlight
moments.body: Ingenhousz, the empress's physician, shows plants only restore air in sunlight — and not at night. He doesn't see leaves; he sees photosynthesis.

moments.title: Calvin's tracer cycle
moments.who: Melvin Calvin, James Bassham, Andrew Benson, Berkeley
moments.body: Calvin uses radioactive 14C and paper chromatography to trace the carbon path through photosynthesis. The Calvin (or Calvin-Benson-Bassham) cycle is mapped step by step. Calvin alone wins the 1961 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Photosynthesis is decoded molecule by molecule.

moments.title: Mitchell's chemiosmosis
moments.body: Working in a privately-funded estate lab in Cornwall, Mitchell proposes ATP is made by a proton gradient across membranes. He is ridiculed for years. 1978 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: A privately funded eccentric solves bioenergetics.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Photosynthesis converts ~100 GtC/yr of CO2 into biomass. Synthetic biology aims to improve the efficiency of Rubisco. Artificial photosynthesis for green H2 is a major research target.
now.open_questions: Can we engineer C3 crops with C4 photosynthesis? Can we make artificial photosynthesis competitive with solar PV?

reflection: Mitchell ran his lab on a private estate after being marginalised by academia. How does science treat its eccentrics?
